subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What effect does a logical left shift of 1 place have on an unsigned binary number?
options: It has no effect on the value
questions.explain: Each left shift of one place multiplies an unsigned binary number by 2.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit binary representation of the denary number 200?
How many different values can be represented using 4 bits?
questions.explain: 4 bits give 2 to the power 4 = 16 different combinations.

questions.q: In ASCII, the character 'A' has the code 65. What is the ASCII code for 'C'?
questions.explain: ASCII codes for letters are sequential, so C is 65 + 2 = 67.

questions.q: When digitising sound, what does the sample rate refer to?
options: The length of the sound file
The number of samples taken per second
The number of bits used to store each sample
questions.explain: Sample rate is the number of samples (measurements of the sound wave) taken each second, measured in hertz.

questions.q: What is the denary value of the hexadecimal number 2F?
Why is hexadecimal often used by programmers instead of long binary numbers?
options: Hexadecimal can represent numbers that binary cannot
It uses only the digits 0 and 1
Computers store data directly in hexadecimal
It is shorter and easier for humans to read and less error-prone than binary
questions.explain: Hex is a more compact, human-friendly way to write binary, as each hex digit maps to exactly 4 bits.

questions.q: What is the denary (decimal) value of the binary number 00101101?
What is the result of a logical right shift of two places applied to the 8-bit number 00011000?
questions.explain: Shifting 00011000 right by two places gives 00000110 (24 becomes 6, a division by 4).

questions.q: What is the result of adding the 8-bit binary numbers 01001101 and 00110110?
What is the denary value of the hexadecimal digit A?
questions.explain: In hexadecimal, A represents the denary value 10.

questions.q: What does the term 'metadata' mean when applied to an image file?
options: Extra data stored about the image, such as its dimensions and date created
The actual colour value of each individual pixel
The sample rate of the image
The compression algorithm running on the file
questions.explain: Metadata is data about the file, such as resolution, colour depth and creation date.

questions.q: Which character set uses more bits per character and can therefore represent characters from many of the world's languages?
questions.explain: Unicode uses more bits per character than ASCII, allowing it to represent a very large range of international characters and symbols.

questions.q: A 4-bit binary number is shifted left by 1 place, but the leftmost 1 is lost. What error has occurred?
questions.explain: Losing the most significant bit during a left shift causes an overflow because the result no longer fits.

questions.q: How many bits does a single hexadecimal digit represent?
questions.explain: One hexadecimal digit represents exactly 4 bits (a nibble).

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal value of the binary number 11101010?
questions.explain: 1110 = E and 1010 = A, so the value is EA.

questions.q: What is the effect of increasing the bit depth when sampling sound?
options: It converts the sound to an image
It reduces the number of samples per second
It increases the accuracy of each sample and the audio quality
questions.explain: A higher bit depth allows each sample to be recorded more precisely, improving sound quality but increasing file size.

questions.q: A black-and-white (1 bit per pixel) image is 10 pixels wide and 8 pixels high. What is its size in bytes, ignoring metadata?
questions.explain: 10 x 8 = 80 bits, and 80 / 8 = 10 bytes.

questions.q: Which formula gives the file size of an uncompressed bitmap image (ignoring metadata)?
options: width x height x colour depth (in bits)
questions.explain: Image file size in bits is the number of pixels (width x height) multiplied by the colour depth.

questions.q: Which unit is the largest?
questions.explain: A gigabyte is larger than a megabyte, which is larger than a kilobyte, which is larger than a byte.

questions.q: In a bitmap image, what does increasing the colour depth (bits per pixel) allow?
options: A greater number of possible colours per pixel
A larger number of pixels in the image
questions.explain: Colour depth is the number of bits used per pixel, so more bits means more possible colours.

questions.q: Which of these is most likely to use lossless compression?
options: A ZIP archive of a text document that must be exactly restored
A heavily compressed JPEG photo for a website
questions.explain: Text in a ZIP file must be restored perfectly, so lossless compression is used.
